news.headline: Famous Hippo Moo Deng Becomes an Aunt!
news.body: Moo Deng, the bouncy baby pygmy hippo who became famous online, is now an aunt! Her older brother Moo Toon and his partner Moo Manao welcomed a healthy baby on November 4 at Khao Kheow Open Zoo in Thailand. The newborn is already walking around and exploring while mom stays close by. Zoo vets are keeping an eye on the pair, and the zoo hasn't picked a date yet for visitors to meet the new baby.

news.headline: NASA Shows Off a Brand-New Test Plane
news.body: NASA unveiled its newest experimental airplane, the X-70 Fractal, at Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Pilots will fly it to test new ways of steering and controlling aircraft, and scientists can quickly swap different experiments in and out. It can fly up to 45,000 feet high, which is higher than most passenger jets. NASA hopes to take it on its first flight within the next two years.

news.headline: Running a Mile While Solving Puzzle Cubes
news.body: A speedcubing champion from the UK named George Scholey set a Guinness World Record by solving a puzzle cube, sprinting one lap around a track, and doing it again and again until he had run a whole mile. He solved four cubes and finished in 5 minutes and 9 seconds! After his final lap, he jumped into his friends' arms to celebrate.

fun_fact: Pygmy hippos are only about 3 feet tall, close to the size of a big dog. They live in the forests and swamps of West Africa. 🦛

this_day_in_history: On November 7, 1867, scientist Marie Curie was born in Poland. She became the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, and the first person ever to win two! 🔬
did_you_know: A puzzle cube can be mixed up in more than 43 quintillion ways, but scientists proved any scramble can be solved in 20 moves or fewer! 🧩
